tag: Cuba, decanted — café culture in a bottle.
d: Aged Cuban rum, infused with island-grown cocoa, coffee and Cuban chilli — a tribute to the café culture that runs through Havana from sunrise to last orders. Nothing artificial. No colouring. No shortcuts.
notes: Roasted cacao, dark espresso, dried fig.
Burnt-sugar sweetness; a slow build of clove, cinnamon and tobacco leaf.
Dry and long. Bitter chocolate that lingers.
serve: Pour neat over a single large rock, or stir into a coffee-forward old fashioned with a swatch of orange peel.

tag: Smoke, oak, conviction.
d: A whiskey designed to pair with smoke and char — built around heavier oak, gently peated malt and a long, mineral finish. A smooth Tennessee rye, peated and sherry-finished, born from one of Asia’s most celebrated wood-fired kitchens.
notes: Charred oak, dried apricot, a thread of campfire smoke.
Toffee and baked apple up front; warm leather and a gentle peat hum behind.
serve: A smoked highball with a long lemon swatch, or neat with a single large rock alongside something off the grill.

tag: The oldest tequila house still in family hands.
d: Extra Añejo — three years in oak. Dried fruit, vanilla, baked sugar. From Casa San Matías, distilling in the Jalisco highlands since 1886.
notes: Oak, chocolate, vanilla, hazelnut, roasted almond and dried fruit.
Full-bodied and sweet at the start — caramel, vanilla and brown spice over cooked agave.

tag: The collector’s bottle.
d: Casa San Matías’ prestige extra añejo tequila, presented in its distinctive sun-face decanter. A centrepiece for the serious collector.

tag: Peru, in a single glass.
d: The blend. Lime, orange and jasmine on the nose; dried nuts and blond tobacco in the mouth. Built for every cocktail — from the Tacama vineyard in Ica, with roots in the 1540s.
notes: Lime zest, orange peel and jasmine.
Bright and clean, with dried nuts and blond tobacco under the fruit.
serve: A Pisco Sour: Acholado, fresh lime, sugar syrup and egg white, shaken hard and finished with a few drops of Angostura bitters.

tag: 100% agave. 100% Jalisco.
d: A clean, peppery 100% agave blanco from the Jalisco highlands — the bartender’s choice for a Tommy’s Margarita.
notes: Cooked agave, fresh lime zest, a snap of white pepper.
Clean and peppery, with a green vegetal lift and a long, citrus-driven mid-palate.
Dry and saline. The mineral signature of the highlands.

tag: Cane, straight from the field.
d: The classic white. Fresh-cut grass, green banana and lime — made for the Caipirinha.
notes: Freshly cut cane, green grass, lime peel.
Bright and lively — sugarcane sweetness, green banana and a peppery edge.
Clean and fresh, with a faint vegetal snap.

d: Six months in American oak — softer agave, vanilla and dried herbs. The bartender’s pick for a Paloma.

tag: 100% agave. 100% Jalisco.
d: A year in oak. Dried fruit, baked apple and gentle cinnamon — made for a slow tequila old fashioned.

tag: Louisville-born. Bar-built.
d: Caramel, baking spice and charred oak — a high-rye bourbon built for cocktails. More rye means more pepper and spice, and a drink that still tastes of whiskey.
notes: Caramel, vanilla, cinnamon, a whiff of orchard fruit.
Rich and warm — toasted oak, dried apple, baking spice from the rye.
Long and lightly drying, with a final note of dark chocolate.
serve: An Old Fashioned with demerara and orange peel — the rye in the mash means the cocktail almost builds itself.

tag: Single-estate Jamaican rum, since 1670.
d: Cane to bottle on one estate in Lluidas Vale, Jamaica. Nothing added. Ever.
notes: Dried banana, baked pineapple, vanilla and warm oak.
Rich and lifted — tropical fruit, a thread of funk, brown sugar and clove.
Long, dry, mineral. The signature of Lluidas Vale.
serve: Neat in a Glencairn, or in a rum old fashioned with demerara and a flamed orange peel.

tag: Jamaican overproof, from Worthy Park.
